pr_title: Fixed pkey amethod double decreases issue in egine framework.
pr_body:
Fixed pkey amethod double decreases issue in engine framework.
Fixes: #20505
pr_comments: Thanks for your support here, it seems OpenSSL doing well, I will close this PR.

issue_context.title: [OpenSSL 3.0 Engine] ECX KEY references count issue
comments: @mattcaswell any ideas about this one? It appears to function the same as  the RSA case, I am not sure why the code was changed..
Thank you for the help, this information really helps me a lot to solve my issue!

review_comments: This looks a bit hacky. I don't see any evidence of this kind of engine change for other key types such as RSA and EC keys, so I am not sure why we would accept it here.

Just like what I explained in #20505, in OpenSSL 1.1.1, the EVP_PKEY_free() will only decrease the reference of the ECX_KEY one time at the beginning of entry point. Because the amethod isn't null, so it will finally invoke the ecx_free() to free the pkey. But in OpenSSL 3, the reference of the pkey not only decreased at the entry point of EVP_PKEY_free(), but also decreased again in ecx_free(), which invokes the ossl_ecx_key_free(). That's why I changed the code here. 

I don't know why the ecx_free() should be changed like this in OpenSSL 3, if you have any idea to solve the issue #20505, please let me know, thanks!

This will only introduce a leak of the `ECX_KEY` since `EVP_PKEY_free` frees the `EVP_PKEY` now, but the reference to the `ECX_KEY` is lost forever.  The real fix is not inside OpenSSL, but inside the engine.

Doesn't this increase the size of `ECX_KEY`?  Everybody who adjusted an engine from OpenSSL 1.1.1 to OpenSSL 3.x had to copy this structure since it is not public.  So if you change anything here, almost all engines will break again.
